title: AI Is Taking Over Physics and Nobody Talks About It
research:
The transcript is Sabine Hossenfelder's video (Aug/Sept 2026) and closely matches her own Substack post 'Conscious Feedback, Roasted Dinosaurs, & The End of Mathematics' (Aug 19, 2026, https://sciencewtg.substack.com/p/conscious-feedback-roasted-dinosaurs), which links each math-community source. Findings:

(1–2) Jacobian conjecture: Levent Alpöge, a mathematician at Anthropic, announced on X (July 19, 2026) an explicit 3-variable counterexample credited to Claude Fable 5, disproving the conjecture in dimensions ≥3 (2D still open); conjecture dates to 1939 / '87-year-old' (https://theconversation.com/hello-there-the-jacobian-conjecture-is-false-thanx-why-a-tiny-social-media-post-has-mathematicians-rethinking-ai-283883, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacobian_conjecture, https://terrytao.wordpress.com/2026/07/21/a-digestion-of-the-jacobian-conjecture-counterexample/, https://www.coindesk.com/tech/2026/07/21/claude-s-fable-5-just-solved-an-87-year-old-math-problem-and-it-matters-for-bitcoin).

(3) OpenAI published (Aug 1, 2026) 'Ten Advances in Mathematics and Theoretical Computer Science' claiming its unreleased Astra model solved/advanced ten problems open ≥10 years, with Lean 4 certificates, no peer review yet (https://thenextweb.com/news/openai-astra-model-ten-math-proofs-non-sofic-groups, https://qz.com/openai-astra-model-math-problems-lean-proofs-080326, https://the-decoder.com/openai-announces-its-next-major-model-astra-by-dropping-ten-previously-unsolved-math-solutions/).

(4) A separate ChatGPT-based conjecture disproof is documented: DataCamp notes a math-olympiad veteran got GPT-5.6 Pro to break the Dinitz–Garg–Goemans conjecture (~1990s, i.e. ~30 years old) (https://www.datacamp.com/blog/claude-fable-5-jacobian-conjecture).

(5–8) Names in Sabine's Substack: graduate student Tasmin Chu (Caltech) calls math in 'existential crisis' and demands a moratorium on using LLMs to prove novel theorems (https://tasmin.substack.com/p/more-calls-to-action-for-the-mathematical, https://proofsandprompts.com/2026/08/09/the-ai-dissenter-viewpoint/, https://siliconreckoner.substack.com/p/news-rumors-gossip); assistant professor Max Weinreich's preprint 'The crisis of AI-generated mathematics' argues for total opposition to AI in mathematics (https://arxiv.org/html/2608.02859v1); postdoc Alexis Marchand ('Mathematicians, machines, and the Earth', proofsandprompts) opposes LLMs on environmental/climate grounds (related Proofs and Prompts posts cite 'unconscionable cost to the environment', https://proofsandprompts.com/2026/09/04/on-proof-and-progress-in-mathematics-in-the-age-of-generative-llms/); PhD student Kirwin Hampshire's 'The Dark Night of Mathematics' says 'I am going insane' and 'suffering a profound spiritual crisis' (https://mathgames.substack.com/p/a-critique-of-the-dark-night-of-mathematics).

(9) Daniel Litt (Toronto; earlier listed as assistant professor, later reported simply as 'professor') gave a talk 'The End of Mathematics' at an OpenAI summit, blogged Aug 11, 2026, describing a future of AI-produced correct results nobody reads (https://www.daniellitt.com/blog/2026/8/11/the-end-of-mathematics/, https://dnyuz.com/2026/08/19/this-may-be-the-first-academic-profession-to-see-its-work-taken-over-by-ai/).

(10, 22) Peter Woit's 'HEP-TH and AI' post (Aug 16, 2026; updated Sept) plots hep-th submissions for May, June, July 2026 and concludes the rate is 'about 1/3 higher this year than in previous years', with August up 49% (https://www.math.columbia.edu/~woit/wordpress/?p=15818). hep-th is indeed arXiv's high energy physics – theory category.

(11–13) Gerardo Adesso is a University of Nottingham quantum-information theorist with prior ChatGPT-assisted publications (https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1002/aaai.12113). I could not locate the specific 2026 preprint directly; the only corroboration found is a secondary summary of this very video stating Adesso used ChatGPT 5.6 to prove there is no shortcut to a class of entangled states and then verified every step himself (https://www.startuphub.ai/ai-news/ai-research/2026/physicists-use-llms-skip-the-panic). Plausible and consistent.

(14–15) Maxwell (1873 Treatise) remarked on the number of electrostatic equilibrium points; formalized in 2007 by Gabrielov–Novikov–Shapiro as the bound (n−1)². Arathoon, Ball & Kvalheim, 'The Maxwell Conjecture is False' (arXiv:2607.27197, July 29, 2026) exhibit five charges with ≥24 non-degenerate critical points; reports state the authors disclosed the construction idea came from GPT-5.6 Sol (https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.27197, https://www.datacamp.com/blog/gpt-5-6-sol-and-maxwell-conjecture, https://officechai.com/ai/gpt-5-6-sol-helps-mathematicians-prove-that-150-year-old-maxwell-conjecture-is-false/).

(16–20) The specific silicon-membrane/laser paper, multi-LLM hep-th computation paper, Claude numerics paper, ion-transport software and ChatGPT-agent stellarator work were not individually located, but the same list appears in the derivative summary of this video (startuphub), and Woit's comment thread independently documents hep-th researchers using Claude heavily for numerics and symbolic computation (Zohar Komargodski, Emil Martinec, Chethan Krishnan comments), plus Anthropic's 'vibe physics' work by Matthew Schwartz — making such papers highly plausible.

comparisons.claim: Claude Fable 5 helped find a counterexample to the Jacobian conjecture.
The Jacobian conjecture had been an open problem since 1939.
OpenAI announced 10 results from its still unreleased model called Astra, each of which either solved or advanced long-standing open mathematical problems.
A group used ChatGPT to disprove a 30-year-old conjecture.
Graduate student Tasman Chu called for a moratorium on using LLMs to prove novel mathematical theorems.
Assistant Professor Maximilian Reich wrote a preprint arguing for total opposition to the use of artificial intelligence in mathematics.
Postdoc Alexis Machete argued that LLMs are evil because they contribute to the climate crisis.
PhD student Kerwin Hampshire stated he is suffering a profound spiritual crisis due to AI developments in mathematics.

Assistant Professor Daniel Litt gave a talk about the end of mathematics, arguing that AI will lead to the production of mathematically correct results that no one will read, care about, or benefit from.
The arXiv category hep-th stands for high energy physics theory.
Gerardo Adesso is a physicist at the University of Nottingham.
Gerardo Adesso proved that there is no easier way to create certain complicated entangled quantum states, and he did so with the help of ChatGPT 5.6.
Gerardo Adesso stated that the AI made a central contribution to developing the proof strategy for his result on entangled quantum states.
James Clerk Maxwell proposed a rule for how many equilibrium points (where electric forces cancel) can arise from a given number of electric charges.

Three researchers showed that Maxwell's rule for the number of equilibrium points from a collection of electric charges is wrong, and their paper states the key idea behind the construction was suggested by ChatGPT 5.6.

Two researchers studying how tiny silicon membranes behave when illuminated by a laser developed a model derived with the help of Claude Fable 5, and the model has excellent agreement with observations.
A paper in high energy physics used several large language models to carry out symbolic and high precision numerical computations.
A paper in quantum physics used Claude for numerical calculations.
A team had Claude write software for moving ions around inside a quantum computer.
In fusion research, a ChatGPT agent was used to decide which stellarator designs to try next.
Anthropic announced that Claude had made a major advance on the Riemann zeta function, working towards the Riemann hypothesis.

Peter Woit examined the number of submissions to the arXiv preprint server in the category hep-th (high energy physics theory) and found that submissions were up about 30% in May and June compared to previous years.
